name: Google Workspace
summary: One Google Cloud project and OAuth client covers every Workspace toolkit; the scopes you request decide whether Google reviews the app and whether a yearly security assessment applies.

capabilities.label: Read email
capabilities.alternative: No non-restricted way to read mail; gmail.metadata is restricted too.

capabilities.label: Open files users pick
capabilities.alternative: Google recommends this scope for most Drive use.

capabilities.label: Read all Drive files
capabilities.alternative: Use drive.file (non-sensitive) if users can pick files.

capabilities.label: Manage tasks
capabilities.alternative: tasks.readonly if the agent only reads tasks. Treated as sensitive until the console says otherwise.

paths.label: Your Workspace organisation only
paths.drivenBy: Internal apps are exempt from verification and the 100-user cap; only accounts in your organisation can connect, and an organisation admin may need to approve the app.
paths.next: Create the project inside your organisation and connect today.

paths.label: External users, non-sensitive scopes
paths.drivenBy: Only non-sensitive scopes, so no scope review; brand verification shows your app name and logo on the consent screen.
paths.next: Publish and connect users today, then submit brand verification so they see your name.

untilApproved.text: Without brand verification the consent screen shows your domain, not your app name.

paths.label: External users, sensitive scopes
paths.drivenBy: A sensitive scope (for example gmail.send or calendar.events) means Google reviews the app before it can leave Testing.
paths.waitOfficial: 3–10 business days; Google's own pages disagree
paths.next: Submit verification this week and build in Testing mode meanwhile.

untilApproved.text: Testing: up to 100 test users, and their access expires 7 days after consent.
Published but unverified: at most 100 new users, behind an “unverified app” warning.

paths.label: External users, restricted scopes
paths.drivenBy: A restricted scope (for example gmail.readonly or drive.readonly) needs verification plus a security assessment by an authorised lab, renewed every 12 months.
paths.waitOfficial: ~6 weeks of review, not guaranteed, plus 1–3 weeks with the lab
paths.costNote: Paid to the assessment lab, not Google; price depends on the lab and assessment level.
paths.next: Submit verification this week — it is the long pole. Keep Gmail on Composio's managed app until you are approved.

untilApproved.text: Testing: up to 100 test users, and their access expires 7 days after consent.
Published but unverified: at most 100 new users, behind an “unverified app” warning.

prereqs.text: A Workspace organisation that owns the project
Public homepage and privacy policy on your own domain
prereqs.why: Not behind a login. Allow time for legal review.
Needed to verify it in Search Console.

prereqs.text: A redirect endpoint on that domain
prereqs.why: Google verifies every redirect domain; the agent writes the 302 route to Composio.

prereqs.text: Budget and an owner for the yearly security assessment
prereqs.why: $540–6,000 a year depending on lab and level.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: console.cloud.google.com → New project. For an internal app, create it inside your Workspace organisation. There is no API for this step.

steps.title: Fill in branding
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Branding: app name, support email, logo, homepage, privacy policy and authorised domains. The agent prepares the values from your site; you paste them.

steps.title: Set audience to Internal
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Audience → Internal. Only accounts in your organisation can sign in.

steps.title: Set audience to External and add test users
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Audience → External, publishing status Testing. Add up to 100 test users.

steps.title: Add only the scopes you use
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Data access → Add or remove scopes. Requested-but-unused scopes are a common rejection reason.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Clients → Create client → Web application. Paste the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config. The client secret is shown once: copy it now.

values.label: Composio redirect URI (default in auth configs)

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: The agent creates a custom auth config with your client ID, secret and scopes through the Composio API, then returns a test connect link.

steps.title: Connect an account in your organisation
steps.detail: Open the connect link and sign in with a Workspace account from your organisation.

steps.title: Connect a test user
steps.detail: Use an account listed as a test user. Its access lapses 7 days after consent, so reconnect before demos.

steps.title: Route the redirect through your domain
steps.detail: Google verifies every domain in your redirect URIs and you cannot verify composio.dev. Add an endpoint on your domain that 302-redirects to Composio, then use that URL in both the Google client and your auth config.

values.label: Redirect endpoint (Next.js route)

steps.title: Verify your domain in Search Console
steps.detail: Add a DNS TXT record for the domain that hosts your homepage, privacy policy and redirect endpoint. Propagation can take hours.

steps.title: Add the Limited Use disclosure
steps.detail: Required for sensitive and restricted scopes, on your app or website. The agent drafts it; you publish it on the verified domain.

values.label: Disclosure (Google's example wording)
values.text: The use of information received from Google Workspace scopes will adhere to the Google User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the consent screen with your app name, then each requested scope in use. Mismatches between scopes, code and video are the most common reason for another round. The agent writes the shot list.

steps.title: Write scope justifications
steps.detail: One reason per scope, tied to a feature users see. The field allows about 1,000 characters. The agent drafts; you edit.

steps.title: Submit brand verification
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Verification centre → Submit.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform → Verification centre → Submit, with the video link and justifications.

steps.title: Google reviews the app
steps.detail: Status shows in the Verification centre. Rejection notes do not always arrive by email, so check it weekly and reply in the same thread.

steps.title: Pass the security assessment
steps.detail: Google sets the assessment level. Pick an authorised lab, run the scan, fix findings, and send the lab's letter to Google. Repeat every 12 months.

steps.title: Switch your auth config to your client
steps.detail: Publish to production. New connections use your client; existing users stay on the old auth config until they reconnect, so the agent drafts the reconnect message.

gotchas.text: Test users must reconnect every 7 days while the app is in Testing.
Google's FAQ describes the 100-user cap as lasting the project's lifetime, while another page says quotas “might be adjusted”. Plan as if it is permanent.
The client secret is shown once, and clients unused for six months are deleted.
Users can untick scopes on the consent screen. Handle partial grants.
Google keeps at most 100 refresh tokens per account per client and silently revokes the oldest.
Customers' Workspace admins can limit Gmail and Drive to trusted apps.
Adding a sensitive or restricted scope after approval likely means another review.

blockers.cause: The client's redirect URI differs from your auth config
blockers.fix: Copy the exact URI from the auth config into the client

blockers.see: Access blocked: app has not completed verification
blockers.cause: The user is not a test user while the app is in Testing
blockers.fix: Add them as a test user, or finish verification

blockers.cause: A redirect, homepage or policy URL is on a domain you have not verified
blockers.fix: Route the redirect through your domain and verify it in Search Console

blockers.cause: The consent screen or a scope's use is not shown
blockers.fix: Re-record from the shot list, one scope at a time
Fix, rescan, and send the new report to the same lab

aiPolicy.summary: User-facing features such as AI summaries of the user's own mail are allowed; using Workspace data to train generalised AI models is prohibited.

customerAdminNote: Workspace admins can limit Gmail and Drive to trusted apps. Send them your client ID to trust before rollout.
unknowns: Whether adding a new sensitive or restricted scope after approval needs a full re-review.
Your exact assessment price: labs quote per app and level.
Google's Tasks API docs do not classify the tasks scopes; this guide treats them as sensitive.
